title: Crypto-Contagion or Safe Haven? Systemic Risk Spillovers Between Digital Assets and Traditional Financial Markets in Latin American Emerging Economies
content: Whether cryptocurrencies function as safe haven assets or contagion amplifiers during financial stress episodes remains an open question in Latin American markets. This paper investigates systemic risk spillovers between Bitcoin and Ethereum and the stock markets of Chile (IPSA), Colombia (COLCAP), and Peru (S&P/BVL) across four stress episodes: COVID-19 (2020), the Russia-Ukraine war (2022), the FTX collapse (November 2022), and the AI-market shock of January 2025. Using DCC-GARCH and CoVaR tail-risk estimation, we find that: (1) Bitcoin and Ethereum function as weak diversifiers in normal periods but generate significant contagion during cryptocurrency-specific crises; (2) the FTX collapse generated the strongest contagion across all three markets (ΔCoVaR range: −2.14% to −4.02%), exceeding COVID-19 spillovers; and (3) Chile demonstrates systematically lower crypto-equity correlation than Colombia and Peru, consistent with its higher institutional quality. These findings have direct implications for portfolio diversification and macroprudential regulation in Latin American financial systems.
